# pistol perft positions, v1 — the movegen oracle's positions (game rules 3, 4
# and 5).
#
# Pinned by SHA-256 in crates/pistol-core/tests/perft_tests.rs
# (PERFT_POSITIONS_SHA256). Editing this file without updating that constant is
# a red test, which is the point. Pass threshold, pre-registered: every case,
# every stated depth, EXACT equality — the engine's count, this file's count,
# and the count an independently written brute-force generator produces, all
# three the same number. A perft that is off by one is a movegen that is wrong,
# and there is no partial credit on it (CLAUDE.md rule 7, docs/decisions.md
# D-12).
#
# Format. One block per case; `plies` accumulates and `expect` is given once per
# depth:
#
#   case <name>
#   plies <q,r> <q,r> ...          stones in play order, repeatable
#   expect depth <n> turns <n>     how many distinct sequences of <n> TURNS the
#                                  position has, repeatable, once per depth
#
# `#` starts a comment line. Anything else is a loader error naming the line: a
# fixture that is quietly half-read is worse than no fixture.
#
# A position is written as the game that reaches it, not as a heap of stones.
# The move list is the canonical position encoding (docs/decisions.md D-6), and
# replaying it means the fixture states only positions a legal game can arrive
# at, with both readings of the rules replaying it for themselves (D-42). Turn 1
# is one stone and every later turn is two, so a ply list groups as 1, 2, 2, …
# and every case but the last one ends at a turn boundary.
#
# What is counted is TURNS: one unordered pair of distinct cells, or the single
# stone that turn 1 (rule 3) and rule 4's truncation make a whole turn. The two
# orderings of a pair are one turn.
#
# Depths. The branching factor is the size of rule 5's legal region squared over
# two, and the region is 217 cells around a lone stone: the counts below are
# measured, and they say that one stone at the origin already has 42768 turns
# and a five-stone cloud 54228. A second full level is that number times the
# next one — around 9 * 10^9 turns for the smallest midgame case here, which no
# test run can enumerate. Depth 2 is therefore stated only where it is
# reachable (a decided position, which has no turns at all), and the second
# level is checked instead by a divide over a deterministic sample of first
# turns, exactly, against the same reference. That is a measured structural
# fact about this game, not a gap in the oracle (CLAUDE.md rule 5's finding, not
# failure).

# One stone on the board: the position every game passes through, and the
# smallest legal region there is — a single radius-8 ball, 217 cells, 216 of
# them empty. Its 42768 turns are the pairs among those 216 plus the pairs whose
# second stone is reachable only through the ball the first one opens.
case one_stone_at_the_origin
plies 0,0
expect depth 1 turns 42768

# A five-stone cloud at a turn boundary, white to move: overlapping balls, so
# the region is a union that is strictly smaller than the sum of its parts.
case tight_cluster_at_a_turn_boundary
plies 0,0
plies 1,0 2,0
plies 0,1 1,1
expect depth 1 turns 54228

# Two lobes joined by a bridge, white to move. White's turn-2 pair 8,0/16,0 is
# legal in exactly one order — 16,0 is sixteen cells from the only stone on the
# board and becomes legal only through the ball 8,0 opens (docs/decisions.md
# D-6) — so the fixture exercises that rule on the way in as well as at the
# position it reaches.
#
# Two DISJOINT clouds are not reachable in a legal game: every stone is placed
# within eight of an existing one, so the region a game builds is always
# connected. The union this exercises is the shape a game can actually make —
# lobes with a waist — and an implementation that measured from one stone, from
# the centroid, or from a bounding box gets it wrong.
case two_lobes_joined_by_a_bridge
plies 0,0
plies 8,0 16,0
plies 16,1 8,1
expect depth 1 turns 162538

# Black to move with five in a row and both ends open: two cells complete the
# line. Rule 4 makes each of them a turn of ONE stone, and neither is half of a
# pair — while a pair whose SECOND stone completes the line is an ordinary turn
# and is counted as one.
case a_win_the_mover_can_take
plies 0,0
plies 0,2 1,2
plies 1,0 2,0
plies 3,2 4,2
plies 3,0 4,0
plies 0,3 2,3
expect depth 1 turns 78072

# Black completed a line on the first stone of turn 7; the second stone of that
# turn was never played (rule 4). A decided position has no turns, at any depth:
# won lines are counted where they end and are never expanded.
case already_won_is_not_expanded
plies 0,0
plies 0,2 2,2
plies 1,0 2,0
plies 4,2 6,2
plies 3,0 4,0
plies 0,4 2,4
plies 5,0
expect depth 1 turns 0
expect depth 2 turns 0
